notes.isolation: Every probe ran with HOME redirected into a throwaway sandbox; the host's real ~/.claude files were never read or written. Auth traveled by inherited environment only.
notes.cross_source_order_evidence: 2.1.283 run: P2's SessionStart pair fired project-first (~1.8 ms) and its Stop pair project-first (~2.5 ms); P6's Stop triple fired user ...331.795 -> project ...331.797 -> relay ...331.799 (~4 ms spread) - run-dependent order again visible across pairs in one evening. The dedicated sleeping-hook probe (Arm S of scripts/probe-stop-edge-contracts.sh, 2026-09-26 against this same 2.1.283): project hook sleeping 300 ms (measured wall 305.5-308.7 ms) vs relay hook 0 ms - the two hooks ran concurrently in 12/12 event pairs and the relay started before the project hook in 4/12 (S1 Stop, S4 SessionStart, S5 SessionStart, S6 Stop). Concurrency, not ordering, is the guarantee - same shape as 2.1.282 (12/12 concurrent, 6/12 flips) and 2.1.270.
notes.tui_per_turn_evidence: Two turns in one TUI session (probe-tui-second-turn.sh): turn 1 fired 1 Stop with reply rendered (35.9 s), turn 2 fired 1 Stop with SECOND-OK rendered (12.7 s); verdict "once-per-turn confirmed", TUI screen showed "(running Stop hook)". The tool-using TUI arms (probe-1 T2 and Arm T) produced incomplete turns this evening - no reply and no Stop within their 270 s / 205 s windows - which per the maintenance doc are re-run shapes, not findings (the same -p arms all completed); the dedicated TUI probe carried the contract cleanly.
notes.degraded_path_hazard: Historical (2.1.270): on runs where the model's tool calls are permission-DENIED (no allowlist, headless), one run out of two produced an extra Stop firing. Re-measured against 2.1.282 on 2026-09-25 (claudepr-d9553d38, Arm D): 15 completed denied runs across three invocations, every one exactly one Stop. Re-measured against 2.1.283 on 2026-09-26 (Arm D): 5/5 completed denied runs in one invocation - all exit 0, stop_hook_active false, the model's own reply confirming its Bash calls were blocked - and every run fired exactly one Stop; the hazard again did not reproduce. Kept on record as historical (mechanism unexplained, small samples; not reachable in the NEEDLE fleet - claude-print.yaml passes --dangerously-skip-permissions). The single-fire poller keeps its tolerance: first payload -> transcript retry/fallback, watchdog bounds the session.
notes.print_mode_tool_use_evidence: Two sequential permitted Bash rounds in one -p run (Arm P): exactly 1 Stop at the turn's true end (payload last_assistant_message: DONE, stop_hook_active: false, single session id), claude exit 0. The unallowlisted T1 arm also completed (exit 0) with exactly 1 Stop of its own.
notes.cutoff_evidence: A -p run cut off by --max-turns fires no Stop of its own: T3 (--max-turns 2, exit 1) added zero firings on 2.1.283, exactly as on 2.1.282, 2.1.281 and 2.1.270 - cutoffs belong to the --stop-hook-timeout watchdog, not the Stop poller.
